paperMetadata.title: Scaling Multilingual and Cross-Lingual Models with Transformers

abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of scaling multilingual and cross-lingual models to better accommodate low-resource languages. We propose a novel architecture integrating language-specific adapters with a unified transformer model, enhancing both multilingual understanding and cross-lingual transfer capabilities. Our approach leverages a dynamic adapter selection mechanism, which provides language-agnostic representations and facilitates zero-shot learning. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, our model demonstrates significant improvements over state-of-the-art multilingual transformers, showcasing superior performance in low-resource settings and retaining competitive accuracy in high-resource environments. Our contributions include a scalable model architecture, a refined training paradigm for low-resource languages, and insights into language-agnostic representation learning. This work sets a new standard for multilingual NLP, providing a robust framework for future research in cross-lingual understanding.

contributions.title: Dynamic Adapter Selection Mechanism
contributions.description: Introduces a mechanism for dynamically selecting language-specific adapters based on context, optimizing model performance across diverse languages.
contributions.novelty: This approach is novel in its ability to adapt language processing dynamically without retraining the entire model, thus enhancing scalability.

contributions.title: Unified Transformer Architecture
contributions.description: Presents a unified architecture that integrates language-specific adapters seamlessly into a single transformer model, facilitating efficient multilingual processing.
contributions.novelty: Unlike existing architectures, our design unifies language adapters within the model, reducing redundancy and improving computational efficiency.

contributions.title: Improved Cross-Lingual Transfer Learning
contributions.description: Demonstrates enhanced cross-lingual transfer capabilities by leveraging language-agnostic representations, notably improving zero-shot learning performance.
contributions.novelty: Our method surpasses traditional transfer learning techniques by focusing on language-agnostic embeddings, which are less explored in current models.

methodology.problemFormulation: The task is to design a scalable multilingual model that effectively handles both high-resource and low-resource languages while enhancing cross-lingual transfer capabilities.
methodology.approach: We develop a transformer model with integrated language-specific adapters that dynamically adjust based on input, using a shared language-agnostic representation layer.

components.name: Transformer Core
components.role: Processes input tokens using self-attention mechanisms.
components.details: Standard transformer layers with multi-head attention, feed-forward networks, and layer normalization.

components.name: Language-Specific Adapters
components.role: Facilitate language-specific processing without retraining the entire model.
components.details: Lightweight modules inserted into transformer layers, activated dynamically based on input language.

components.name: Adapter Selector
components.role: Determines which adapters to activate based on linguistic context.
components.details: Employs a gating mechanism informed by input language embeddings and contextual signals.

assumptions: Assumes availability of language-specific data for training adapters.
Assumes that language-agnostic layers can generalize across languages.
limitations: Performance may degrade if adapters are poorly trained for specific languages.
The model's size may grow with the number of adapters, impacting efficiency.

evidence.description: Evaluates multilingual performance on standard benchmark datasets.

setup.context: Assessing performance across multiple languages including low-resource ones.

evaluation.protocol: Compare performance metrics across test datasets in various languages.

results.notes: Improved over baseline models by 3.4 points.

evidence.analysis: The experiments demonstrate a consistent advantage in low-resource scenarios, validating the effectiveness of language-specific adapters.

evidence.description: Tests cross-lingual transfer capabilities in zero-shot settings.

setup.context: Evaluate zero-shot performance on unseen languages.

evaluation.protocol: Measure accuracy on test sets of languages not present during training.

results.notes: Significantly higher than baseline zero-shot models.

evidence.analysis: The model's ability to leverage language-agnostic representations proves crucial for effective cross-lingual transfer.

Develop methods to train adapters efficiently, reducing computational overhead and enhancing scalability.
